Azariah (son of Jehu)
az-uh-RYE-uh
proper noun
Hebrew ’Azaryah (H5838), “the LORD hath helped” or “whom the LORD aids,” the son of Jehu in the house of Jerahmeel of Judah (1Chr 2:38-39); one of many men named Azariah in the sacred record.

Biblical Definition

Azariah is the son of Jehu in the Jerahmeelite branch of Judah, set in the descent that runs through Obed and Jehu unto Helez and beyond: “And Obed begat Jehu, and Jehu begat Azariah, And Azariah begat Helez, and Helez begat Eleasah” (1Chr 2:38-39). The reader should mark that Azariah is among the most common names in all the sacred record, borne by many men — a high priest in Solomon’s day, a king of Judah who is also called Uzziah, one of Daniel’s three companions renamed Abednego, and many more (1Ki 4:2; 2Ki 15:1-7; Dan 1:6-7). This Azariah is none of those, but the genealogical figure of the second chapter of Chronicles, a single link in the house of Jerahmeel. His name is a whole confession: “the LORD hath helped.” Set in a bare register of begettings, it preaches the truth that carried the tribe of promise across the centuries: that the help of every household of Judah was the LORD Himself, who kept the line unbroken when no man could have kept it. The Chronicler writes Azariah down because the LORD knoweth them that are His (2Ti 2:19), and the help that named him is the same help that brought the tribe at last to the Son who sprang out of Juda (Heb 7:14). His name is written, and the names of all the helped of God, in the book of remembrance (Mal 3:16).

Webster 1828 Definition

The son of Jehu in the house of Jerahmeel of Judah, one of many men named Azariah in Scripture.

expand to see more

AZARIAH, the son of Jehu in the Jerahmeelite branch of Judah.

The name signifies “the LORD hath helped” or “whom the LORD aids.”

He stands in the descent that runs through Obed and Jehu unto Helez and Eleasah.

He is one of many men named Azariah, and is the genealogical figure of 1 Chronicles 2.

His name is kept by the Chronicler among the households of the tribe of promise.

Key Scripture

1Chr 2:38 — "And Obed begat Jehu, and Jehu begat Azariah,"

1Chr 2:39 — "And Azariah begat Helez, and Helez begat Eleasah,"

2Ti 2:19 — "Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity."

Mal 3:16 — "Then they that feared the LORD spake often one to another: and the LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the LORD, and that thought upon his name."

Modern Corruption

A man of Scripture’s register, not a contested doctrine; his name confesses that the LORD hath helped His people.

expand to see more

Azariah the son of Jehu is a name in the genealogy of Judah, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine him. The dictionary records him that the reader may know him for the genealogical figure of the second chapter of Chronicles, and not confuse him with the many other men named Azariah in the sacred record.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the LORD hath helped His people, and that He knoweth them that are His (2Ti 2:19). A name set in a bare register confesses the help of God; and the help that named this man is the help that kept the tribe of promise whole, and that brought it at last to the Christ who sprang out of Juda.

Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “the LORD hath helped,” Azariah names the son of Jehu in the house of Jerahmeel.

Azariah — Hebrew ’Azaryah (H5838), “the LORD hath helped” or “whom the LORD aids.”

He was the son of Jehu in the Jerahmeelite branch of Judah.

He stands in the descent through Obed and Jehu unto Helez and Eleasah.

He is one of many men of Scripture named Azariah.

Usage

"Like Azariah, whose name means “the LORD hath helped,” the believer’s whole history is the help of God."

"The LORD who helped the households of Judah is the same who keeps His people now."

"His name and the names of all the helped of God are written in the book of remembrance."
